rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window and avoid truncation. This should show whether any compounds are unretained or only elute during the high-organic hold, giving a strong basis for narrowing the window and tuning slope next.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain is reducing t_last by concentrating the gradient around the observed elution window and making it steeper. The estimated elution solvent strengths span roughly 0.18 to 0.68, so this narrower, shorter gradient should pull the last peak closer to 10 min while likely preserving ample resolution.

Resolution is still comfortably above target, so push for a faster fully resolved method by slightly increasing final organic, shortening the gradient, and raising temperature one step. This should bring the last peak under 10 minutes while likely keeping all pairs above 1.5 given the large current resolution margin.

We already have the maximum CRF, so now the goal is to find the shortest method that still keeps every pair at or above 1.5 resolution. Cutting tG one step while keeping the same window and temperature is the cleanest way to test how much time margin remains before the first critical pair fails.

The same method at 4 minutes still has comfortable margin, with the first pair remaining the limiting one. Shortening to the minimum gradient time directly tests whether we can keep full resolution while further reducing run time; if pair 1–2 drops below 1.5, we can step back.

At 2 minutes only the first pair fails, so lower phi0 one step to retain and spread the earliest peaks while leaving the rest of the window unchanged. This specifically targets pair 1–2 with minimal impact on total run time, probing whether the fastest fully resolved method can still be achieved at tG = 2.

Changing phi0 downward did not help the critical first pair, so test a slightly narrower and less steep window by lowering phi1 one step at the same 2-minute gradient. This may recover enough resolution for pair 1–2 while keeping the run much faster than the proven 4-minute method.

The critical pair improves as the 2-minute gradient is made shallower, so lower phi1 one more step to further reduce slope while keeping all peaks within the gradient/hold window. This is the most direct remaining test for a fully resolved 2-minute method.

Now that a 2-minute method is fully resolved, test whether one higher temperature can reduce run time while maintaining the slim but acceptable margin on the first pair. This directly probes whether temperature helps or hurts the critical selectivity at the fastest gradient.

Higher temperature hurt the critical first pair, so stay at 45 C and make the 2-minute gradient slightly shallower again by lowering phi1 one step. The goal is to increase the pair 1–2 margin above 1.53 while still keeping t_last under 10 minutes, which should preserve CRF 1.000 with a more robust fast method.

The 2-minute, 55% final organic method is the best fast condition so far, and higher temperature worsened the critical first pair. Lowering temperature one step may improve that selectivity and provide extra resolution margin while still keeping the last peak under 10 minutes.

At 40 C the 2-minute method has strong resolution margin but just misses the 10-minute target, so raise phi0 one step to reduce overall retention and pull the last peak slightly earlier. This should test whether we can keep the first pair above 1.5 while recovering full CRF 1.000.

The current 2-minute, 40 C method remains fully resolved with some margin on the first pair, so raise phi0 one step to reduce retention further and see if the run can be compressed even more without dropping pair 1–2 below 1.5.
